execution.routing_reason: Independent implementation review uses the configured review role.

contract_checks: Contract-conformance checks were run by OpenAPIContractCodeGenerator against contract version 1.0.0.
The review status is derived only from the severity of the findings those checks produced.
The changed source of 2 repositories was read and compared.

cross_repository_findings.description: The console hard-codes the CSV columns it will accept before ever submitting to the server, instead of deriving them from (or keeping them in sync with) the single-app create schema as the contract mandates. The backend derives ACCEPTED_COLUMNS dynamically from `addAppSchema.appDetails`, whose fields (per the single-app createApp service code) include at least app_type, app_developer, app_title, app_url, icon, store and app_id — but never publisher_name, which is taken from the authenticated user, not the CSV. The console's static list omits app_type/app_url/icon and wrongly includes publisher_name. Because the console blocks the Upload button whenever its client-side validator reports any problem (including UNKNOWN_COLUMN), a CSV containing the columns the backend actually requires (app_type, app_url, icon) will be rejected client-side before it ever reaches the server, and a CSV that follows the console's own accepted list (including publisher_name) will be rejected by the server with BULK_APPS_UNKNOWN_COLUMN.
cross_repository_findings.evidence: Console: `const BULK_APPS_ACCEPTED_COLUMNS = ['app_id','app_title','store','app_developer','publisher_name'];` and `const problems = validateBulkAppsCsvText(csvText); if (problems.length) { setClientProblems(problems); return; }` (blocks submit). Backend: `const appDetailsSchema = appValidation.addAppSchema.extract('appDetails'); const ACCEPTED_COLUMNS = Object.keys(appDetailsSchema.describe().keys).filter(...)` combined with service code `const { app_type, app_developer, app_title, app_url, icon, store: appStore } = appDetails;` showing appDetails (and hence ACCEPTED_COLUMNS) includes app_type/app_url/icon and excludes publisher_name.
cross_repository_findings.recommended_fix: Remove the hard-coded BULK_APPS_ACCEPTED_COLUMNS list from the console (or fetch/derive it from the same source of truth used server-side, e.g. expose the accepted column list via an endpoint or a shared config), and drop publisher_name while adding app_type/app_url/icon (or whatever the actual single-app appDetails schema requires) so the client-side pre-validation cannot diverge from the server's authoritative BULK_APPS_UNKNOWN_COLUMN check.

cross_repository_findings.description: The contract specifies status_code 409 for BULK_APPS_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE, but the validation module throws this code with a hard-coded statusCode of 400 whenever only in-file duplicates (no row-validation errors) are detected.
cross_repository_findings.evidence: Contract: `{ "code": "BULK_APPS_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE", "status_code": 409, ... }`. Backend: `const code = rowErrors.length === 0 && duplicateErrors.length > 0 ? 'BULK_APPS_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE' : 'BULK_APPS_ROW_VALIDATION_FAILED'; throw createBulkCreateAppsError(code, 400, 'One or more CSV rows failed validation', {...});` — the statusCode argument is always 400 regardless of which code is chosen.
cross_repository_findings.recommended_fix: Pass 409 as the statusCode when the resolved code is BULK_APPS_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE (and keep 400 for BULK_APPS_ROW_VALIDATION_FAILED) so the emitted HTTP status matches the approved contract.

payload.compatibility_assessment: OpenAPIContractCodeGenerator reported at least one blocking contract-conformance finding; see cross_repository_findings. The changed source of 2 repositories was reviewed together. The two workstreams implement complementary halves of the same bulkCreateApps feature and mostly agree on method, path, content type, size/row limits, and response/error envelope shapes. However, the console's client-side CSV pre-validation hard-codes an accepted-column list that was not derived from (and does not match) the backend's actual accepted-column set, which is dynamically derived from the single-app create schema. This causes the console to block valid uploads and/or let through uploads the backend will reject, undermining the 'browser-side hint only' assumption the console code documents for itself.
payload.security_assessment: NOT PERFORMED. This gate inspects no repository source and makes no security claim about the coordinated change. Each repository's own 007_review.json carries the security assessment for its diff.
